name: MN-04
label: Safe D

McCollum's overwhelming fundraising edge ($1.45M raised vs $63K) and no outside opposition

model.rationale: Every available signal aligns: the district's 18-point Democratic lean, McCollum's roughly 23-to-1 fundraising advantage, absent outside spending against her, and market pricing near 96% all point to a comfortable Democratic hold, so the Safe D rating stands.
model.watch: Only a major scandal, a dramatic national wave against Democrats, or significant outside spending for Wikstrom could put this seat in play.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Minnesota's 4th District leans heavily Democratic, and Betty McCollum is a long-serving incumbent seeking another term. She enters the general election with a large financial edge, roughly $1.4 million raised and about $497,000 on hand, while Republican Paul Wikstrom has raised about $63,000. No outside groups are opposing her, and prediction markets put Democratic odds near 96%.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this district, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the incumbency advantage, and the money gap. Those all point the same direction, toward a comfortable Democratic win in a seat with an 18-point Democratic lean. Wikstrom would need a dramatic shift in the national environment or an unexpected campaign development to make this race competitive.
